title: Inquest set 16 months after woman's death; B.C. Civil Liberties boss blasts long wait
article: A coroner's inquest into the death of a 42-year-old woman in the Prince George RCMP jail cells will be held more than 16 months after she died, the Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor-General announced Tuesday.
The inquest into how Cheryl Ann Bouey died on June 26, 2008, will be held at the Prince George Law Courts from Nov. 2 to 6, before coroner Rodrick MacKenzie.
The B.C. Civil Liberties Association criticized the delay, saying inquests involving in-custody deaths, which are mandatory in B.C., should be held much faster.
"Delays like this are completely unnecessary," said David Eby, executive director of the BCCLA.

"There's a systemic issue here. It's not just this case. It's every police-involved death, as far as we can tell, where family and involved police officers and police departments need to wait more than a year at least before the file can be closed."

MacKenzie and a jury will publicly hear evidence from witnesses in order to determine the facts surrounding the death. The jury will make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths under similar circumstances.
Bouey was arrested, along with her common-law spouse, for public intoxication in the parking lot outside the College Heights Pub, Prince George, around 12:40 a.m. on the day she died.
A report prepared by the RCMP in Ottawa last year revealed that 56 per cent of in-custody deaths happen in B.C., even though only about one-third of the force is stationed here.
There have been three high-profile cases of deaths in police custody in northern B.C. in recent years: Ian Bush in Houston, Kevin St. Arnaud in Vanderhoof and Donald Lewis near Williams Lake.
